newsitem.title: USA: Ascend stock jumps on upbeat comments.
newsitem.headline: Ascend stock jumps on upbeat comments.

text.p: Stock in computer network company Ascend Communications Inc. jumped nearly 14 percent after executives told analysts they predicted broad demand with little price pressure through the end of the year.
The company's stock rose $6.375 to $53.125 in heavy trading of more than 24 million shares. Ascend, based in Alameda, Calif., makes high-speed digital networking gear.

"We continue to see fairly broad-based demand both internationally as well as domestically for Internet services," Bernie Schneider, vice president of strategic business Development, said in an interview after the analyst meeting.

"We're feeling pretty good about what Ascend's opportunities are based on current market demand," Schneider said following the presentation by senior executives. "If anything. demand's getting a little bit better."

Schneider said the company has virtually completed the integration of Cascade Communications Corp., and the combined companies should be able to exploit opportunities created in Europe from deregulation of telecommunications.
Ascend said June 30 it had completed the purchase of Cascade and that the deal will be accretive to earnings in 1998.

"We expect to maintain gross margins in the 65 percent range through the end of the year," Schneider said, adding the company has seen a slowing down of price-cutting actions, and expects prices to stabilise through the end of the year.
"We're just not going to see the level of price cutting that we've seen historically on list prices," he said.
"We've seen the competitors kind of coalesce around a certain point, and through the end of the year we're not expecting to see significant change in the prices."

Schneider said a lot of the company's international business is with telephone companies and large Internet service providers, which involve larger sales cycles but are large deals. He said Ascend believes most of its customers in Europe are planning "fairly major upgrades" over the next two quarters.
